name: Bowling Green
start_event: Common Council leased the old parade ground before the fort as a bowling green in 1733, the city's first public park (the dataset's 1686 is the Dongan Charter)
planting_note: Iron fence of 1771 still stands; statue of George III stood 1770-1776; relandscaped several times, last with the subway and plaza works of the 1970s

name: City Hall Park
start_event: Grounds laid out as a park around the new City Hall, occupied 1812; the land was the town Common from the 17th century (dataset: 1867)
planting_note: The Common held an almshouse, jail and barracks in the 18th century; Croton fountain 1842; the south end was lost to the Post Office 1869-1939 and restored after its demolition; rebuilt 1999

name: The Battery
start_event: Public promenade on the old gun battery; Fort George was demolished by 1788 and its rubble used to extend the shore (dataset: 1870)
planting_note: Castle Clinton built offshore 1808-1811 and joined to the park by landfill 1853-1872, which roughly doubled the Battery; elevated railway loop over the park 1877-1940; closed in part for the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel 1940-1952

name: Washington Square Park
start_event: Washington Military Parade Ground declared in 1826 on the potter's field used 1797-1825; made a public park 1827
planting_note: Marsh of Minetta Brook, then potter's field 1797-1825 (about 20,000 burials); redesigned with curving paths 1870-71; arch 1892 (marble replacing the wooden one of 1889); closed to traffic 1959

name: Union Square Park
start_event: Opened to the public in July 1839 (land set aside 1831-33)
planting_note: Oval fenced garden with fountain 1842 (Croton water); redesigned by Olmsted and Vaux 1872 as a meeting ground; raised and rebuilt over the subway concourse 1928-1929

name: Madison Square Park
start_event: Opened 10 May 1847 on part of the old parade ground
planting_note: Relandscaped 1870 by William Grant and Ignaz Pilat; restored 1999-2001

name: Tompkins Square Park
start_event: Square acquired 1834 and opened as a park in 1850 (dataset: 1834)
planting_note: Salt meadow of the Stuyvesant farm, filled 1830s; stripped as a parade ground 1866-1878 and replanted 1879; elms survive from that planting

name: Stuyvesant Square
start_event: Land given by Peter Gerard Stuyvesant in 1836; fenced 1847 and formally opened 1850 with its fountains (dataset: 1836)
planting_note: Two fenced halves divided by Second Avenue; cast-iron fence of 1847

name: Bryant Park
start_event: Reservoir Square designated 1847 beside the Croton Distributing Reservoir (1842)
planting_note: Potter's field 1823-1840; Crystal Palace stood here 1853-1858; park laid out 1871; renamed Bryant Park 1884; reservoir replaced by the Public Library 1900-1911; rebuilt as a formal lawn 1934 and restored 1988-1992

name: Marcus Garvey Park
start_event: Opened as Mount Morris Park in 1840 around the rock outcrop the grid could not cross (renamed 1973)
planting_note: Fire watchtower 1856; landscaped by Ignaz Pilat 1867-1871; recreation centre and pool 1930s-1969

name: Central Park
start_event: Greensward Plan chosen April 1858; the Lake opened to skaters in December 1858 (land taken 1853-1856)
planting_note: Built in stages: clearing of Seneca Village and other settlements 1857; the Lake and the south end 1858; the Ramble June 1859; everything south of 79th Street open by late 1860; Bethesda Terrace 1859-1864; extended from 106th to 110th Street 1863; north end and Harlem Meer 1860s; declared complete 1876. Planted on blasted and filled ground. The Lower (Receiving) Reservoir of 1842 was drained 1930 and became the Great Lawn 1934-1937

name: Prospect Park
start_event: First section opened to the public 19 Oct 1867 (construction from July 1866; land acquired from 1860)
planting_note: Olmsted and Vaux; Long Meadow and east side first, the Lake dug 1867-1871, substantially complete 1873; the Ravine keeps older woodland

name: Grand Army Plaza
start_event: Laid out 1867 as the Plaza, the entrance to Prospect Park
planting_note: Berms planted to screen the oval; Soldiers' and Sailors' Arch 1892; Bailey Fountain 1932

name: Eastern Parkway
start_event: Built 1870-1874 to Olmsted and Vaux's design, the first parkway (dataset: 1898)
planting_note: Six rows of trees on two malls from Grand Army Plaza to Ralph Avenue

name: Ocean Parkway Malls
start_event: Built 1874-1876 from Prospect Park to Coney Island (dataset: 1869, the enabling act)
planting_note: Tree-lined malls with the first bicycle path in the country (1894)

name: Fort Greene Park
start_event: Washington Park established 1847 on the site of Fort Putnam (1776) and Fort Greene (1812)
planting_note: Redesigned by Olmsted and Vaux 1867 with the crypt for the prison-ship dead; renamed Fort Greene Park 1897; Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument 1908

name: Riverside Park
start_event: Land taken 1872; Riverside Drive and the upper slope opened 1880 (dataset: 1876)
planting_note: Olmsted's plan of 1873-1875 for the slope from 72nd to 125th Street; railway along the shore until the West Side Improvement of 1934-1937 roofed the tracks and added filled land, the promenade and the 79th Street boat basin

name: Morningside Park
start_event: Built 1883-1895 on the cliff the grid could not use (land acquired 1870)
planting_note: Olmsted and Vaux plans of 1873 and 1887; retaining wall and stairs by Jacob Wrey Mould 1883-1892; pond made 1989-1990 in the pit of the cancelled Columbia gymnasium (1968)

name: Van Cortlandt Park
start_event: Title taken 12 Dec 1888 under the New Parks Act of 1884
planting_note: Van Cortlandt estate with the house of 1748; lake dammed about 1699; first public golf course in the country 1895; parade ground 1901; cut by three parkways 1930s-1950s

name: Pelham Bay Park
start_event: Title taken 12 Dec 1888 under the New Parks Act of 1884
planting_note: Former estates and salt marsh; Orchard Beach built 1934-1937 on fill that joined Hunter Island and Rodman's Neck to the mainland; landfill at Tallapoosa Point 1963-1978

name: Bronx Park
start_event: Title taken December 1888 under the New Parks Act of 1884
planting_note: Lorillard estate along the Bronx River gorge with old-growth forest; New York Botanical Garden established 1891 on the north half; Bronx Zoo opened 8 Nov 1899 on the south half

name: Forest Park
start_event: Brooklyn bought the land 1895-1898 as Brooklyn Forest Park
planting_note: Oak forest on the terminal moraine; drives by Olmsted Brothers 1890s; golf course 1901; Jackie Robinson (Interboro) Parkway cut through 1933-1935

name: Seward Park
start_event: Opened 17 Oct 1903 with the first permanent municipally built playground in the United States (land condemned 1897)
planting_note: Tenement blocks cleared 1897-1900

name: Thomas Jefferson Park
start_event: Opened 7 Oct 1905 (land acquired 1897)
planting_note: Tenement and industrial blocks cleared; pool 1936

name: McCarren Park
start_event: Opened 1906 as Greenpoint Park (land acquired 1903-1905); renamed 1909
planting_note: Pool opened 1936, closed 1984, reopened 2012

name: Kissena Park
start_event: City acquired the Parsons nursery land from 1906; park opened 1910 (dataset: 1924)
planting_note: Kissena Lake; grove of exotic trees left from Samuel Parsons' nursery

name: Coney Island Beach & Boardwalk
start_event: Riegelmann Boardwalk opened 15 May 1923 with the public beach built out by sand fill (dataset: 1938)
planting_note: Beach widened with pumped sand 1922-1923; boardwalk extended to Brighton Beach 1926 and 1941

name: Inwood Hill Park
start_event: Officially opened 8 May 1926 (land assembled 1915-1941)
planting_note: Last natural forest and salt marsh on Manhattan; estates and institutions removed 1930s; Henry Hudson Bridge and parkway cut through 1936

name: Fort Tryon Park
start_event: Dedicated 12 Oct 1935 (John D. Rockefeller Jr. gave the land in 1931)
planting_note: Built 1931-1935 by Olmsted Brothers on the Billings and other estates; heather garden and terraces; The Cloisters opened 1938

name: Alley Pond Park
start_event: City acquired the land in 1929; park opened 1935 (dataset: 1934)
planting_note: Kettle ponds, old forest and salt marsh; Alley Pond itself was filled for the Cross Island Parkway and Long Island Expressway interchange

name: Randall's Island Park
start_event: Park and stadium opened 11 Jul 1936 with the Triborough Bridge (the city bought the island in 1835 for its institutions)
planting_note: House of Refuge, hospitals and asylums 1840s-1930s; Little Hell Gate between Randalls and Wards islands filled in the 1960s

name: Flushing Meadows Corona Park
start_event: World's Fair opened 30 Apr 1939 on the cleared Corona ash dumps; turned over as a city park 3 Jun 1967 (dataset: 1934)
planting_note: Salt marsh of Flushing Creek, ash dump about 1909-1934; graded 1936-1938 with two artificial lakes; fairs 1939-1940 and 1964-1965 (Unisphere); United Nations General Assembly met here 1946-1950

name: The High Line
start_event: First section (Gansevoort to 20th Street) opened June 2009 (the city took title in 2005-2006)
planting_note: Freight viaduct of 1934, disused 1980; later sections opened 2011, 2014 and 2019; self-seeded vegetation replaced by Piet Oudolf's planting

name: Brooklyn Bridge Park
start_event: Pier 1 opened 22 Mar 2010 (dataset: 2001)
planting_note: Cargo piers 1-6 of the 1950s rebuilt as parkland in stages to 2021

name: Freshkills Park
start_event: First section inside the landfill, North Park Phase 1, opened October 2023 (the dataset's 1929 is the acquisition of the marsh)
planting_note: Tidal marsh; landfill April 1948 - March 2001 (reopened for World Trade Center debris 2001-2002); mounds capped and planted with grassland in stages from the 1990s; the whole park is planned for the 2030s

name: Trinity Churchyard
start_event: Churchyard of Trinity Church, chartered 1697 (oldest dated stone 1681)
planting_note: Burials ended in the 1820s except in vaults

name: St. Paul's Chapel Churchyard
start_event: Churchyard of St. Paul's Chapel, opened 1766

name: First Shearith Israel Graveyard
start_event: Burial ground of Congregation Shearith Israel at Chatham Square, in use from 1683
planting_note: Reduced to a fragment when the Bowery was widened

name: New York Marble Cemetery
start_event: Incorporated 1830, the first non-sectarian burial ground in the city
planting_note: Lawn over 156 underground marble vaults

name: Moravian Cemetery
start_event: Opened 1740 at New Dorp
planting_note: Enlarged with the Vanderbilt land in the 1860s-1880s (Vanderbilt mausoleum 1886, grounds by Olmsted)

name: Green-Wood Cemetery
start_event: Incorporated 18 Apr 1838; first burial 1840
planting_note: Rural cemetery by David Bates Douglass on the terminal moraine (Battle Hill); enlarged to 478 acres by the 1860s; gates 1861-1865

name: Trinity Church Cemetery and Mausoleum
start_event: Opened 1843 by Trinity Church on part of John James Audubon's land at 155th Street
planting_note: Divided when Broadway was cut through in 1871

name: Calvary Cemetery
start_event: First burial 31 Jul 1848 (the Alsop farm, bought by St. Patrick's Cathedral trustees 1845)
planting_note: Second, Third and Fourth Calvary added to the east 1867-1900

name: Cypress Hills Cemetery
start_event: Opened 1848
planting_note: National cemetery section 1862

name: The Evergreens Cemetery
start_event: Incorporated 1849
planting_note: Laid out by Andrew Jackson Downing and Alexander Jackson Davis

name: Woodlawn Cemetery
start_event: Incorporated 1863; first burials 1865 (burial year not confirmed in the cited article)
planting_note: Laid out on the landscape-lawn plan from 1867

name: New York Botanical Garden
start_event: Chartered 1891 on the northern 250 acres of Bronx Park
planting_note: Conservatory 1899-1902; keeps the 50-acre Thain forest, uncut woodland along the Bronx River

name: Bronx Zoo
start_event: Opened 8 Nov 1899 in the southern part of Bronx Park
planting_note: Astor Court 1899-1910

name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
start_event: Opened 13 May 1911 on land set aside in 1897 (a former ash dump)
planting_note: Japanese garden 1915; cherry esplanade 1921-1941

name: Duane Park
start_event: Bought by the city from Trinity Church, the first land the city acquired specifically for a public park; the Parks dataset dates the acquisition 20 Jun 1797, Wikipedia 1795
planting_note: Triangle replanted 1887 by Vaux and Parsons and restored 1999

name: St. John's Park
start_event: Private square laid out by Trinity Church in the first years of the 19th century before St. John's Chapel (1803-1807); sold to the Hudson River Railroad in 1866 and built over with a freight depot 1867-1868
planting_note: Fenced garden for the surrounding householders, planted from the 1820s; the site is now the Holland Tunnel exit plaza

name: Gramercy Park
start_event: Deeded by Samuel B. Ruggles to trustees for the lot owners in 1831; fenced 1833
planting_note: Swamp drained and filled 1831-1833; planted 1844; still a private, locked park

name: Hamilton Fish Park
start_event: Opened 1900 with a gymnasium by Carrere and Hastings (land acquired 1896-1897)
planting_note: Tenement blocks cleared; rebuilt 1903; pool 1936

name: Poe Park
start_event: Opened 1902 opposite Edgar Allan Poe's cottage, which was moved into the park in 1913 (dataset: 1896)

name: Corlears Hook Park
start_event: Opened 1905 (land acquired 1893)
planting_note: Shoreline moved outward by the East River Drive and East River Park, 1930s

name: De Witt Clinton Park
start_event: Opened 1905 with the first children's farm garden in a city park (land acquired 1901-1902)
planting_note: Lost its western edge to the West Side Highway

name: Riverbank State Park
start_event: Opened 27 May 1993 on the roof of the North River sewage treatment plant
planting_note: Planting in shallow soil over the plant deck

name: Gantry Plaza State Park
start_event: Opened May 1998 on the Hunters Point car-float yards
planting_note: Extended north 2009; float-bridge gantries of the 1920s kept

name: Hudson River Park
start_event: Created by the Hudson River Park Act of 1998 on the piers and bulkhead left by the cancelled Westway; the first section, in Greenwich Village, opened about 2003
planting_note: Opened section by section from 2003; Little Island (Pier 55) 2021, Gansevoort Peninsula 2023

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt Four Freedoms Park
start_event: Opened October 2012 at the southern tip of Roosevelt Island to Louis Kahn's design of 1974
planting_note: Fill of the 1960s-70s; allees of littleleaf lindens

name: Domino Park
start_event: Opened 10 Jun 2018 on the waterfront of the Domino Sugar Refinery

name: Shirley Chisholm State Park
start_event: Opened 2 Jul 2019 on the capped Pennsylvania Avenue and Fountain Avenue landfills in Jamaica Bay
planting_note: Landfills operated 1956-1985; capped and planted with grassland and 35,000 trees and shrubs in the 2000s

name: Little Island
start_event: Opened 21 May 2021 on the site of Pier 54/55
planting_note: Planting on 132 concrete piles over the Hudson
